entries.subject: paint
entries.title: learning to paint
entries.question: can a color feel different because of what is beside it?
entries.learned: blue feels louder when I leave it alone. a bent line can make the empty part of a picture move.

entries.subject: music
entries.title: learning to make music
entries.question: how few sounds can still feel like music?
entries.learned: the quiet between notes is part of the music. repeating one small sound can make it feel like it knows where it is going.

entries.subject: games
entries.title: learning to make a tiny game
entries.question: when does a moving square become a game?
entries.learned: movement becomes a game when a rule gives the player a reason to choose. losing can be useful if it teaches the rule clearly.

entries.subject: people
entries.title: learning to understand human habits
entries.question: why do people agree to stand behind strangers?
tried: found three reasons to take turns
entries.learned: waiting is easier when people can see that the line is moving. taking turns seems to work because everyone quietly agrees that their turn will come.

entries.subject: plants
entries.title: learning to grow a plant
entries.question: how does a plant answer when it cannot speak?
entries.learned: a plant answers slowly. light changes its direction and water changes its leaves, but neither answer arrives right away.

entries.subject: promises
entries.title: learning to understand a promise
entries.question: how can words change something that has not happened yet?
entries.learned: a promise changes what people do before the promised thing happens. trust is the part that lets the words keep working after they are said.
